objective: Prove in Lean (core 4.32.2): (1) a loop of permutation contact closes exactly when the composed permutation has a fixed point, and a bouquet of loops with one selector each allows a selector pattern exactly when the selected holonomies share a fixed point; (2) the selector shape is the nerve of the fixed-point sets, and a minimal non-face is excluded alone, so a minimal non-face of three or more loops is a knot (K1-K3); (3) free contact never binds two loops; (4) a knot among k >= 1 loops needs at least k+1 witness values, and star transpositions on k+1 values achieve it; (5) every simplicial complex is the nerve of fixed-point sets of involutions. In prose: the common-fixed-point rule for general networks, its H^1 reading for free abelian contact, and the memory of uniform group contact as a function of the number of independent loops.
status: Proved by HOLES-COHOMOLOGY-20261019-001B-P001 (Lean 4.32.2, standard axioms, five controls rejected; prose for general networks; census agrees). A loop of permutation contact closes exactly when its holonomy has a fixed point; with one selector per loop, the shape of the loop constraints is the nerve of the holonomies' fixed-point sets; a minimal non-face is excluded alone, so ties and knots among loops are atoms; free contact never binds two loops; a knot among k loops needs k+1 witness values, and star transpositions attain it; every simplicial complex is such a shape. In prose: a network allows a pattern exactly when its holonomy group has a common fixed point; for free abelian contact this is the vanishing of a class in H^1; with uniform group contact the memory depends only on the number of loops; non-free composites record more than the loops' conjugacy classes.
title: What permutation contact remembers (Lean)
